It sets the global Git core.hooksPath and chains pre-existing hooks, then a push to a protected branch waits while a reviewer model reads the committed change through read-only Git tools and asks the developer a question. The reviewer runs in a separate context from the coding agent and never sees the conversation that produced the code, so it grades the diff rather than the prompt. Questions cover behavior, failure modes and invariants rather than file names, and the check is open book: the developer can read the code or ask their agent while answering. A wrong answer produces an explanation plus a new scenario on the same concept, and disputes and errors never count as passing. Five outcomes exist: correct answer, wrong answer, dispute question, pause check, and skip this time, where skips never count as passing. A pass lasts 24 hours unless the code, destination or policy changes; a matching push waits up to 25 minutes, and an agent shell may time out sooner. Question count scales with change size (small changes up to one question, documentation or trivial edits none, large changes up to three at default depth), and a separate distance setting (high for design, low for implementation detail, mixed by default) controls how close questions get to the code. Model review runs on the developer's own Claude Code or Codex plan allowance, on OpenRouter, or on any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; Sphinx has no account or hosted service of its own. A typical check makes about 5 to 8 requests plus roughly one per answer, and there is no default cap on model calls, so 'sphinx config --max-model-calls 30' (range 1 to 100) is available. Supported agents are Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Pi, or plain Git without an agent. Per-repository files created by 'sphinx init' are .sphinxconfig (policy), .sphinxignore (paths never read) and .sphinxcontext.md (short project description sent with every reviewer request), and machine-wide settings live in ~/.config/sphinx/config.json.
